#1923. Celtic know they 'need strengthening' as January transfer intel emerges

Celtic chiefs are hoping the January transfer window comes quickly as they prepare to strengthen Martin O’Neill’s squad.

Around 120 supporters attended a Q&A at Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club, where recruitment, the manager’s future and the club’s longer-term ambitions were among the issues raised.

Speaking on Clyde 1 Superscoreboard, club president Joe Clark revealed that chief executive Michael Nicholson made it clear Celtic are aware of the need for reinforcements. Clark said: “While Martin was there, the question was asked to the board, ‘What are we doing to replace him?’

“They just said Martin is on a one-year contract with an option at the moment. In January there is going to be a budget to spend. The feeling that came out kind of was that everyone was wanting January to come early.

“Michael Nicholson said he wanted January to come quickly. They know they need strengthening. We bought two centre forwards in the summer, and I asked how we came to the conclusion about those two.

"It’s about getting the right people available.”

O’Neill was not initially expected to attend the meeting, with Clark only learning of his involvement after people had already begun arriving. He said: “I got told Martin was coming while I was in the hall, when the first load had already come down.

“Martin has been down at the club recently anyway; it was before he went back to Celtic. He was down doing a Q and A. So it was nice to see him.

“But as you know better than me, when Martin is in the room he usually takes over the room.”

Clark admitted O’Neill’s presence changed the mood and revealed the Celtic boss occasionally stepped in to answer questions that had originally been directed towards the board. He continued: “Yeah, it [having him there] definitely did [change the mood].

"There were times Martin took over the question. The question would maybe be for the board, but he would jump in and take it.

“He did a few circles around when one of our members asked him what the objectives were for the next five years. Winning the league five times, qualifying for the Champions League, winning a game in the Champions League, and qualifying out of the League Phase.

“Martin came back to that a few times as maybe a bit unrealistic. I’m not saying HE said it was unrealistic, but he kept going back and questioning it.

Supporters also questioned how Celtic identify transfer targets and arrive at recruitment decisions. Clark added: “On the football side of things, they got asked a lot of things about how they go about identifying players and how they go and make decisions.

“And they’ve got a four-man panel, and people who meet the criteria get fed into that, then Martin makes the final decision on top of that.”

#1919. This can't go on at Celtic – or can it? O'Neill fears and the McGregor dilemma

Welcome to The Burning Questions, our new daily debate where we take one major subject in Scottish sport and tackle the three questions everyone is talking about.

Each day, our writers will offer their verdicts on the biggest issues and arguments dominating the agenda. And Celtic are first under the spotlight, with plenty to discuss after a difficult period for the club.

Martin O’Neill’s future is one of the major talking points, while a run of just three wins in 10 games has raised fresh questions over Celtic’s form and where they go from here. Is O’Neill the right man for the job in the longer term, and just how concerning has the recent run become?

Then there’s Callum McGregor. If Besiktas win on Thursday night, is it time to give the Celtic captain a European vacation and keep him fresh for the domestic challenges ahead? Liam Bryce and Graeme Young give their answers to today’s three Burning Questions.

A defeat for Celtic against Besiktas would make it three wins in 11 games. It can't go on, can it?

Liam Bryce: It can. Sunday’s defeat to an excellent Falkirk laid bare what has been obvious about this Celtic team for a long time: any sort of coherent gameplan, with some added quality, is enough to cause them major problems.

At home, they might still be able to bully their way past lesser-resourced domestic opponents most weeks, but I wouldn't confidently back them against anyone in Europe at the moment. I'm not rushing to put my house on Besiktas. Celtic are well capable of winning this game. It's just that things have deteriorated to the point that no one would be surprised if they left Glasgow with a victory.

Graeme Young: It can't. If Celtic are pulled apart at the seams by the Turkish heavyweights, then it might be one punch too many for a side who appear dazed and confused every time they enter the field.

Celtic appear incapable of competing against teams packed with pace and power. The good results in the league appear unsustainable and now the domestic form is also going backwards. The swamped fixture calendar ensures it's a long time until January, when transfer salvation may or may not lie.

But, let's be honest, there is a structural issue within this Celtic team, both with and without the ball, which runs deeper than individual personnel.

Martin O'Neill appears to veer from bullish to crestfallen. What has to happen to make his position untenable?

Liam Bryce: An awful lot more than has happened already. I can't see the Celtic board making a change in the dugout unless there's a complete implosion domestically. They will be far more reluctant to sack Martin O'Neill, a club legend, than they were Wilfried Nancy.

The 2020/21 season feels like a decent barometer of what it might take. Celtic had effectively surrendered the league title long before action was taken on Neil Lennon, who was allowed to struggle on for several months. That appointing Nancy mid-season went so badly will likely only make an already conservative hierarchy even more hesitant.

I'm not convinced they will see much cause for concern with O'Neill's side still top of the league. I can't envisage Celtic dropping enough domestic points to take themselves out of a title race, especially against opponents who have deficiencies of their own. O'Neill is going nowhere.

Graeme Young: The fixture gods appear to be in O'Neill's favour after the Besiktas game. The next three are against Kilmarnock and St Mirren at home before a trip to Portugal for a showdown with second-tier Torreense.

It looks less like a gauntlet and more like a get-out-of-jail card after recent setbacks. However, a team on the slide often can't get out of its own way. Perhaps further setbacks are hard to swerve when every fixture now feels fraught with danger.

Is it time for Celtic to see what life after Callum McGregor looks like right now?

Liam Bryce: It would be if there was anyone to take his place. But does that player exist at the moment? I don't think so.

Joel van den Berg has barely been seen and, regardless, is still just 19. Oliver Sorensen, too, remains something of a mystery. He may possess some of the physical qualities that could help plug the midfield gaps that are causing the team so many issues, but does he have the nous to be the fulcrum of the team?

I do feel somewhat for McGregor. There's a significant body of evidence that he is a far better player than we're currently seeing. I don't really buy the narrative that his legs have gone. I'm more inclined to believe he is a victim of an incoherent system.

He has never been a midfield enforcer, or even an Andrea Pirlo type, spraying passes the length and breadth of the pitch. Quick combinations, proficiency operating in tight areas and well-timed bursts forward are his primary attributes, yet he seems reduced to a vehicle for giving the ball to Liam Scales.

But he will need replacing eventually, and Celtic's recruitment seems to have ignored this eventuality.

Graeme Young: If Celtic feel the full force of Besiktas' goalscoring exploits, then it has to be time to spare Callum McGregor for the rest of the European games.

The skipper has been the reference point in the midfield for a decade, the last five years coming with the captain's armband attached. Yes, the lack of an obvious replacement is a strong argument, but there has to be an attempt to try something different.

Any call to revamp the engine room would also benefit the skipper when it comes to league duty over the busy winter period.

#1909. Cristiano Ronaldo announces Portugal retirement after record-breaking 23-year career

Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football.

The 41-year-old made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and has gone on to play 234 times for the national team, scoring 146 goals – both of which are records in the men’s game.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Cristiano Ronaldo (@cristiano)

A post shared by Cristiano Ronaldo (@cristiano)

In a video on social media, Ronaldo said: “To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team.

“I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the honour and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.

“Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart.

“A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.”

Ronaldo’s announcement comes less than a month after he was suspended for 30 days and fined 255 euros (approximately £210) by the Portuguese Football Federation after walking out on the national team.

The veteran forward left the camp shortly before a Nations League game against Denmark following a row with head coach Jorge Jesus.

He did not reference the incident in his farewell video but admitted he had made “mistakes”.

Ronaldo continued: “When I look back at everything I experienced with the national team, I don’t just see matches, goals records or trophies, I see people.

“I see Portuguese people living abroad who, for 90 minutes, felt a little closer to home. I see millions of Portuguese people I have never met but who became part of my life.

From St Andrews to AI: What happens when underlying business assumptions change?

This can't go on at Celtic – or can it? O'Neill fears and the McGregor dilemma

Scotland set to win tug of war for exciting rising star as rival nation to miss out

“Because, at the end of the day, football is so much bigger than a game. Football is about people.

“Throughout my entire career with the national team, I always pushed myself beyond my limits. I wanted to win. I wanted to be better. I wanted to make history. I always demanded the most of myself. I always wanted more.

“I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this shirt. There were perfect afternoons and nights, there were victories I will never forget. There were defeats that still hurt to remember.

“I made mistakes. I suffered. There were also moments where I couldn’t give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up and, above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.”

Ronaldo led Portugal to European Championship victory in 2016 as well as winning the Nations League in 2019 and 2025 but World Cup success eluded him.

“Over the years I learned a few very simple things: goals fade, trophies end up in museums, records are eventually broken, but there is something time can never erase, the place we hold in people’s hearts,” continued Ronaldo.

“If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you embrace someone, forget a worry or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it.

“Thank you for allowing me to live a dream that began when I was just a little boy in Madeira running after a football.

“The number seven shirt will remain. The pride of having worn it will be mine forever. Portugal will always be a part of me. Farewell, until we meet again.”

As MilanNews write, Diawara has gone from a semi-unknown prospect to a potentially key asset in the space of a few weeks. After his strong performance against Udinese and his more difficult performance against Bologna, there was some surprise when he was named as a starter vs. Inter.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Yet, he passed a decidedly more difficult test than anything he has had in his young career to date. It wasn’t a perfect performance, which is inevitable considering his age and inexperience, but it showed the Frenchman can truly become more than just an emergency solution.

The data speaks volumes about the young French defender’s night. Diawara completed all 15 of his attempted passes, finishing with 100% accuracy, even producing a key pass, according to data provided by Wyscout.

In total, the former Troyes player had 31 touches and five defensive contributions, despite being tested by Spence’s pace. Yet, despite this, Diawara didn’t shy away from physical confrontations: he won three out of five ground duels and three out of five aerial duels, with two tackles completed.

In the derby, Diawara demonstrated his ability to play left wing-back, a somewhat unusual role because he has not always been known for his ability to push forward given that he is a more natural centre-back.

Diawara doesn’t have to be an undisputed starter for this Milan side to be a surprise package, but if he can maintain this reliability, he could truly become a valuable asset in extending the rotation possibilities of Ruben Amorim’s side.

#1902. PSG: Who is David Boly, the highly sought-after young prospect who scored against Villarreal?

By Axel Clody | 04 Nov 2026 10:08

Paris Saint-Germain cruised to a 6-0 win over Villarreal on Tuesday night in the Champions League. But, beyond the demonstration, the Paris club saw academy graduate David Boly score the final goal of the game.

Introduced in the 74th minute in place of the captain for the night, Achraf Hakimi, David Boly made his mark four minutes later with a goal full of determination: a run into the Villarreal box and a thunderous strike to beat the unfortunate Peter Gulacsi, who had already been beaten five times.

As relayed by L’Equipe, the young right-back became the second-youngest player in Paris Saint-Germain history to score in European competition, at 17 years and 285 days. The record is held by his team-mate Warren Zaire-Emery, who scored against Borussia Dortmund in 2023 at 17 years and... 280 days.

After the game, David Boly expressed his joy at scoring in front of the media: ‘I receive the ball from Joao Neves, I get in front of the goal and I shoot (smiles). I see that it goes in and, well, it was incredible, honestly.’

But behind the celebrations around the win and the academy graduate’s first goal, one question still remains: will David Boly be Achraf Hakimi’s long-term understudy at Paris Saint-Germain?

As relayed by L’Equipe, the 17-year-old Frenchman is still not a professional. The French club have nonetheless offered him a first contract, with ‘a very high financial proposal’, a sign of confidence from the leaders of Ligue 1 and the Champions League, who also say they no longer want to offer ‘oversized’ contracts.

David Boly has not yet signed, with plenty of competition for his signature: big European clubs and ‘more modest’ sides are interested in the talented youngster.

If Paris Saint-Germain want to tie down the defender, like Quentin Ndjantou, compared to a Formula 1 car by Luis Enrique, his playing time in the coming months will influence the decision he takes.

From the player’s side, it can also be argued that a professional contract is simply a way of monetising his talent: David Boly will always leave Paris Saint-Germain for a higher fee with a contract than without one, with his academy deal ending in the summer of 2027.

The Paris side nonetheless seem to be working hard to show the young talent their confidence: playing time, with two appearances, one in Ligue 1 and one in the Champions League, and a high salary for his potential first contract.

According to L’Equipe, David Boly ‘wishes to continue his career at his youth club’. The trend is therefore towards the contract being signed soon.

But when? And, with such exposure in the Champions League, can the right-back’s entourage keep waiting, hoping for a financial bidding war from the many suitors?

If, with his goal and fine introduction, David Boly pushes a little harder to be Achraf Hakimi’s genuine understudy at Paris Saint-Germain, the very status of understudy behind the best right-back in the world could ultimately lead him to ask another question: could the young academy product not be a starter... elsewhere?

#1901. Mikey Moore trapped in a German nightmare as Rangers loan hero caught in a 'mess'

Mikey Moore’s loan spell at FC Koln has been branded a “mess” by German media with the former Rangers loan star failing to register a goal or assist in his first eight appearances.

Moore - who started Tottenham's Premier League opener before his loan exit - netted seven times and claimed eight assists in 47 outings at Ibrox last season before returning to Spurs and heading to the Bundesliga.

The winger has teamed up in Germany with ex-Celtic defender Jahmai Simpson-Pusey and highly-rated English prospect Reigan Heskey, son of former Liverpool and England striker Emile.

But Moore has been unable to hit the ground running at Koln and was once again forced to settle for a place on the bench for Saturday’s 1-1 draw away to Union Berlin.

Read more: The telling Michael Nicholson quip that reveals Celtic's transfer strategy

The England Under-20 international was introduced as a substitute, but his wait for a first goal contribution in Germany continued. And afterwards, leading German outlet BILD delivered a scathing assessment of his performances so far.

Fellow German outlet Express has gone one step further, claiming Moore is becoming “impatient” over his lack of minutes and suggesting the youngster is simply trying too hard to make things happen when his opportunities arrive.

Koln boss Rene Wagner admits seeing Moore finally break his duck with a goal or assist remains on his “personal bingo card”, although he insists the youngster has already shown enough to suggest he can make a success of his spell in Germany.

Speaking after the draw with Union, Wagner said: “An assist or a goal from Mikey Moore would still be on my personal bingo card.”

Asked about the decision to leave Moore on the bench, he explained: “Mikey started against Schalke and in the cup. He’s already shown from the bench that he can bring a lot of energy. That was the idea. We wanted to become dangerous again late in the game with his substitution.

“We anticipated Union would play with a back five and wanted to have two holding midfielders on the pitch to be able to switch formations effectively. We had to do that after just five minutes.”

#1900. Worst of weather can’t blow Eastbourne Borough’s league campaign off course

Eastbourne Borough claimed three valuable Isthmian Premier points on Tuesday night with a 1-0 victory over lowly Stanway Rovers – but for manager Steve King, it was all about the elements as well as the opposition.

The Sports extended their incredible current run to 14 victories in 15 starts – just the 3-0 FA Cup defeat at Salisbury blotching the record – as they swept aside second-bottom Stanway Rovers at the Connect Management Stadium.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Skipper Josh Rees notched the crucial goal just before half-time, and Borough spurned a whole clutch of chances to make the game safe against gritty opposition, in front of a huddled crowd of 619 – only a little over one-third of Saturday's attendance against Ramsgate.

The victory nudges the Sports up to third in the table, ahead of a potentially difficult trip to Dartford on Saturday.

Borough are, frankly, the team to beat right now, as this compelling campaign moves towards the winter. But for the players, supporters and the gaffer himself, Tuesday night was no feast of football, just a test of endurance.

"Shocking! Not my team, nor even the opposition, but the weather! If you don't know Eastbourne, you don't know our weather. It was horrendous - the wind especially - it's the worst I've ever seen it - and I live in this town!" said King.

"It was appalling and it ruined the game - no flow or pattern. It was just a match that you wanted to be finished, as soon as the referee blew his first whistle.

"But ultimately you just go about your business. Sometimes if you can 'win horribly' like that, it is actually a good sign. We can't always play great football and win. Long throws, headers off the line, you just do what you have to.

"But we did miss five unbelievable chances, and I mean five, to make the game safe. Their keeper has made three or four brilliant saves - but we should be putting those chances to bed.

"Poor as the game was, poor as the conditions were, we've had chances and we should have taken and made the game safe. So I was disappointed from that point of view, but… cross it off, game done. You can only get three points for a win, whatever the quality or the conditions or the opposition."

Is King: the new Michael Fish? Readers of a certain age will just still remember the infamous forecast in 1987 from the BBC weatherman - the night before a hurricane swept across southern England. Michael actually lived in Eastbourne: perhaps he should have known better.

There was no football stadium at Priory Lane back then, but the flat Langney landscape has always been open to all the elements. Never mind, you hardy Borough fans: not even the worst that the Channel throws at us can blow King's Sports off course.

#1899. Cardiff vs. West Ham: Will Scott Parker be in dugout for Championship game after Hammers return?

By Darren Plant | 04 Nov 2026 10:12, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 10:13

West Ham United have announced the appointment of Scott Parker as their new head coach.

On Tuesday morning, the Hammers revealed that they had parted company with Nuno Espirito Santo.

That was despite the club sitting just six points adrift of leaders Middlesbrough in the Championship table, and a game at Cardiff City taking place on Wednesday night.

However, given the speed that reports emerged over an approach for Parker, it soon became apparent that the wheels over a replacement had already been in motion.

Just over 24 hours since Nuno was sacked, the return of former West Ham midfielder Parker has been confirmed.

West Ham have revealed that the 46-year-old will be in the dugout for the game with Cardiff.

Parker told the club's official website: "It is a very proud moment for me to step into this role and return to a Club that means so much to me and my family. A lot of very fond memories of my time here - four years of probably the best football I played in my career.

"There was a warmth, a love, a feeling that I probably didn’t have anywhere else. There was something which stood out constantly and that was the relationship that I built up with the fanbase here. That rapport and respect, that I felt instantly.

"More than anything, this is an opportunity that I am very excited about. I feel privileged and honoured to be the guy that wants to lead us back to the Premier League and be the Head Coach of this Football Club at this moment in time.

"My energy levels, my enthusiasm, my desire, my passion - it’s absolutely running through and that's the feeling I had as soon as there was a conversation that this was possible. That's exactly why I'm here and why I want to be here.

"From my first calls with Karim [Virani] and Daniel [Křetínský], it was clear they have a shared vision and desire to return the Club to the Premier League as quickly as possible. I share that ambition and I’m very confident we can achieve it.

"I’ve been in this division three times and I've got out of this division three times. This is a tough division, there is absolutely no denying it. And I will use every ounce of my experience, every ounce of my knowledge, to have an understanding of what we're going to need to bring consistency.

"And that's going to be the key word for all of us really. The consistency of what we do and the commitment levels that we go to will give us the best opportunity to get out of this division and be the team that we can be."

While there has been occasional criticism of Parker's playing style, he boasts an incredible record as a manager in the Championship.

He has guided each of Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley to promotion to the Premier League.

A total of 76 wins, 41 draws and 21 defeats have been recorded in 138 games in the second tier of English football.

#1898. GdS: How Amorim’s fluidity helped Rabiot record career-best start to a season

Adrien Rabiot continues to deliver in the biggest games for AC Milan, and Ruben Amorim is arguably getting the best ever form out of him.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by recalling how different things were in the summer. With Milan falling to fifth and Massmiliano Allegri being sacked, many presumed that Rabiot could follow him to Napoli, to play Champions League football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Rabiot not only remained at Milanello, but is also the Atlas of the team this year. He carries it on his shoulders and takes its weight with disarming ease and personality. While Allegri observes Milan from below, Adrien has found a new coach who is giving him a new lease of life.

The derby goal is an excellent indicator of Rabiot’s confidence, attempting that billiard-like shot (even though some, like Yunus Musah, maintain it was a cross) in a match like this, with the game still wide open, signifies complete self-confidence.

The Frenchman knows perfectly well he has a powerful shot, but he opted for finesse, guiding the ball to kiss the post and land in the back of the net as eleven Nerazzurri players watched it slowly and mockingly cross their penalty area.

Rabiot was one of the derby’s heroes but has been performing at a high level for several matches now. He currently has the best average rating in the squad, and it’s a stratospheric 6.81 (out of 10, across all games).

The other key number is nine: five goals and four assists this season makes nine contributions, the most in the squad. In the league, he’s been involved in a goal in each of his last five games: assists against Lazio, goals against Lecce and Sassuolo, a goal and assist against Atalanta, and a goal in the derby.

To better understand his further improvement from an already very high level, we must consider that in the entire last season, Adrien had six goals and four assists. He’s one goal away from matching that tally.

Some tactical considerations help contextualise things. Compared to Allegri, Amorim’s style of football is on another level, being much more attacking. It’s not based solely on counter-attacks, but on a flow of play that starts from midfield and allows for the runs of those who move in between the lines.

Rabiot has always been a player who can get forward: he has the physique, technique, and footballing intelligence. Amorim has given him a further step because he’s made him more difficult to read for opponents.

If before, the Frenchman was a classic pivot midfielder, now you find him practically everywhere. At the start of the season, Amorim’s style of football was positional, locked into a 3-4-2-1 that seemed set in stone with Rabiot behind the striker.

Then the Portuguese coach realised he was doing himself harm and began a tactical overhaul. The fundamentalist has become fluid, and the playing system is now an abstract concept that must be filled with individual interpretations.

This is a set of circumstances where Rabiot shines. The derby is a perfect example: the former PSG man was everywhere, depending on his own tendencies and the team’s need for certain characteristics in certain parts if the pitch.

This is the best start to a season of his career. Now, in addition to the pitch, he’ll also have to keep an eye on his desk. After Strahinja Pavlovic and Christian Pulisic, he’s the next one destined to ascend to the fourth floor of Casa Milan to sign a renewal waiting for him.

Findlay Curtis insists he is there for the long run at Rangers and Scotland as he looks to cement his place for club and country.

The 20-year-old attacker, who came through the Ibrox academy, had a successful loan spell at Kilmarnock last season and returned to the Light Blues looking to kick on.

However, he has made most of his recent appearances off the bench as Derek McInnes’s side have gone on a 11-game unbeaten run which has taken them into second place in the William Hill Premiership ahead of the trip to St Mirren on Saturday and secured a place in the Premier Sports Cup final against Hibernian next month.

Despite a lack of recent starts Curtis was named in Sebastien Pocognoli’s first Scotland squad for the Nations League camp in September and October and then dropped to the Under-21s where he starred in the 5–2 victory over Azerbaijan Under-21s at Rugby Park.

Curtis returned to the senior squad and came off the bench in the 2-1 home defeat to Slovenia and on Tuesday it was revealed that he had retained his place in the squad for this month’s final two Group B1 matches against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

The Gers youngster is ready to do whatever it takes to become a regular for the Light Blues and in dark blue.

He said: “He (Pocognoli) just wanted me to be myself. You saw it in the last camp. I was in for the first couple of days and then I dropped down to the Under-21s. I knew I wasn’t going to get enough game time, so I think I had to go and prove myself a bit.

#1896. Council applies for artificial grass pitch in Uckfield to enhance football infrastructure

Mid Sussex Times and Sussex Express reporter

Holly Goring submitted an application to Wealden District Council for the new pitch at Victoria Pleasure Ground at Victoria Pavilion on Old Timbers Lane, New Town.

People can view the application documents at planning.wealden.gov.uk using reference WD/2026/2097/F.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The description said the application is for an artificial grass pitch with perimeter fencing, acoustic fencing, hardstanding areas, a storage container, sports lighting and access pathways.

The agent for it is Surfacing Standards Limited. Their design and access statement said: “The development has been carefully designed to comply with the FA and Sport England guidance, with the intention of enhancing infrastructure. The scheme will provide a modern, durable, and inclusive all-weather sports facility, enabling year-round football activity for both partner club members and the wider community, regardless of seasonal or weather-related constraints.”

The statement said the new AGP would offer improved training and playing surfaces for various age groups and teams. It also said the facility would be available for community use, meaning the site can be a hub for sports and recreational activities. The statement added that the 9,971 square metre site was chosen for its ‘strategic location within a well-established community and its history as a recreational site’.

It continued: “The redevelopment reuses existing open space to deliver much needed grassroots football infrastructure for Uckfield and the wider area.”

It said the proposal has been developed to be sympathetic to its surroundings and said the design ‘reflects best practice in safeguarding, accessibility, sustainability, and local policy alignment’.

The statement said the playing surface would be a 3G artificial grass system that features a 40mm pile, which is ‘partially in-filled with silica sand for stability and granulated rubber for performance’. The artifical grass will be green so it looks like natural grass.

The design statement said: “This surface will be installed over a shockpad and is recognised as the most suitable artificial playing surface for community football and youth football development.”

#1895. Barcelona transfer news: Deco tracks four young centre-backs with Real Madrid and Premier League rivals

By Axel Clody | 04 Nov 2026 10:44

Barcelona are already preparing for their next transfer window with one priority: strengthening their central defence. Sporting director Deco is monitoring four young centre-backs.

The situation is starting to become worrying for Hansi Flick. Andreas Christensen has been out since September with a left thigh muscle injury. Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia are also unavailable, while youngster Xavi Espart must observe a long period of rest after his ankle injury.

Against Alaves, the German manager even had to use Frenkie de Jong at centre-back, alongside Pau Cubarsi.

Although not all of these absences are expected to last, they highlight the fragility of the Barcelona squad. Kounde’s situation is also worth monitoring in the medium term, as his future at right-back is not entirely separate from the club’s thinking on recruitment.

In this context, Deco is looking in particular for a left-footed defender, comfortable in build-up play and capable of defending far from his own goal to complement Flick’s very high defensive line.

According to Sport, three new young players feature in the early thinking of Barcelona’s sporting director.

The first is Vitor Reis. The 20-year-old Brazilian defender belongs to Manchester City and already has European experience, having spent a loan spell at Girona. His athletic profile and technical quality match Barcelona’s requirements. However, it remains to be seen whether he is the ideal choice, as his playing time is very limited, with four appearances and 199 minutes.

Another option from Brazil is Arthur Dias, who plays for Athletico Paranaense. The 19-year-old defender is more of a bet on potential, with the possibility of gradually joining the Catalan club’s rotation. Finally,

Ruud Nijstad of FC Twente completes this first list. The 18-year-old Dutchman is considered a defender with high potential and is also targeted ny Manchester United and Bayern Munich. His room for progression makes him an interesting target for a club that also wants to prepare for the future.

Finally, the name of Youri Baas particularly catches the attention of the Catalan club’s decision-makers. At 23, the Ajax defender already has more experience at the highest level than the other three targets.

Left-footed, strong in duels and able to play at left-back, the Dutchman offers appreciable versatility. His quality in build-up play is also an argument for fitting into Flick’s system.

Under contract until June 2028, Baas will not necessarily be easy to prise away from Amsterdam. His value has risen and several English and German clubs are also following his performances. Real Madrid have also shown an interest in the Dutchman, according to Fichajes, although that option is less current than the one involving Barcelona.

For Deco, the equation will therefore be as much financial as sporting. The salary cap limits Barcelona’s options and could force the club to consider a departure before recruiting. Baas nevertheless appears a particularly coherent option to meet an immediate need, without abandoning a recruitment policy focused on young players.

#1893. Big improvement on Enfield showing – butBurgess Hill Town out of luck at Wingate

The contest at home to Enfield on Saturday was disrupted early on when a kit clash between the sides became apparent. Just five minutes in, play was halted while officials tried to resolve the issue, with Hill switching to white shirts.

The visitors wasted little time in taking control. Thomas Avgoustidis opened the scoring in the 15th minute before Amrit Bansal-McNulty doubled their advantage 10 minutes later.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Goalkeeper Roco Rees produced several important saves and Hill manager Gary Mansell made two changes at half-time in an attempt to turn the contest around, introducing Charlie Lambert and Ben Pope.

But Enfield struck twice after the restart. Avgoustidis added his second in the 48th minute before completing his hat-trick just two minutes later.

Brad Barry and Nicky Wheeler came on but Enfield continued to press forward and added a fifth through Oliver Davis in the 62nd minute. Pope came close to a consolation but Daniel Efobi struck in the second minute of added time to complete the scoring.

On Tuesday night, luck was not on the Hillians’ side as they conceded an agonisingly late equaliser at Wingate & Finchley, despite an exceptional display of hard work and resilience. The performance was a clear improvement on Saturday’s heavy home defeat.

The Hillians started the first half on the front foot, and this positive approach continued throughout the opening 45 minutes as they looked the more likely side to break the deadlock.

They produced some excellent passages of play, creating several promising half-chances for Ben Pope and Charlie Lambert, with the latter coming closest to opening the scoring. With five minutes remaining in the first half, Pope was shown a yellow card. Moments later, the half-time whistle sounded with neither side able to find the breakthrough.

As the second half got underway on a cold evening in North London, the Hillians continued to take the initiative, creating further opportunities to open the scoring.

Lambert came close before Yoan Edoukou flashed a shot across goal from inside the box, which agonisingly went wide of the far post just before the hour mark.

As the half progressed, Roco Rees was called into action just before the 75-minute mark, producing an excellent save to keep the scores level. Shortly afterwards, Chris Whelpdale was introduced in place of Charlie Lambert.

Then, with 80 minutes played, the Hillians won a corner, which was delivered by Edoukou towards the near post. Whelpdale, with his first touch, connected brilliantly with a header that sailed over the goalkeeper and into the net, giving the Hillians a deserved lead.

Following the goal, Burgess Hill defended resolutely, with Harry Lawson producing a last-ditch block to prevent the hosts from drawing level.

With 90 minutes played and a minimum of six minutes of added time indicated, the Hillians made another substitution, with Jake King replacing Yoan Edoukou. However, with virtually the last action of the game, the hosts were awarded a penalty, which Ryan Lowe converted to make it 1-1 at full time.

It was heartbreak for the Hillians, who had been the better side throughout and looked deserving of all three points, only to leave with just one.

Nevertheless, there were plenty of positives to take from the performance, particularly following Saturday’s result. The hard work, determination and resilience shown by the players were there for all to see, and the boys should take great pride in their efforts on this occasion.

As always, a huge thank you goes to the travelling Hillians supporters who made the journey to North London. Your tremendous support is, as ever, greatly appreciated.

Next up for the Hillians is another away trip on Saturday, when they travel to Chatham Town FC for a 3pm kick-off.

#1892. Everton vs. Coventry City: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of Premier League clash

By Matt Law | 04 Nov 2026 10:47, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 10:48

Everton will welcome Coventry City to the Hill Dickinson Stadium in the Premier League on Friday night.

The Toffees are currently seventh in the Premier League table, boasting 13 points from nine matches, while Coventry are currently 16th in the division.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides ahead of their contest in Gameweek 10.

Everton and Coventry have locked horns on 80 previous occasions, with the former leading the overall head-to-head record 37 wins to the latter's 23, while there have also been 20 draws.

This is a fixture that dates back to March 1910, when Everton beat Coventry 2-0 in the FA Cup.

Fast forward to the present day, the last meeting between the two teams came in the Premier League in January 2001, with Everton posting a 3-1 success over Coventry.

However, Coventry have actually won two of their last three meetings, including a 2-1 victory when the pair last locked horns at the home of Everton in December 2000.

There have been 18 previous Premier League meetings between Everton and Coventry, with the latter posting six wins to the latter's three, while there have also been nine draws.

Everton have only won one home Premier League match against Coventry - a 2-0 success at Goodison Park back in April 1999.
